Manufacturing / Case study

From manual calculations to a working production platform.

A custom incentive system that gives production, managers and HR a defined path from entry to approval.

6operational modules5-level approval workflow

Capabilities involved

  • Custom software
  • Process discovery
  • Operational reporting

One calculation. Several departments to reconcile.

A cable manufacturer needed production-incentive calculations and approvals to work across departments. Spreadsheet-based work made the roles, rules and reporting requirements difficult to manage consistently.

Put the rules and approval responsibilities into the system.

The software had to represent the actual rules of the operation. Production users, IT, managers and HR needed their responsibilities translated into a workflow they could review and use.

PRODUCTION / WORKFLOW
One process. Clear responsibilities.
01
Production entryCapture the shift and calculation inputs
02
Manager reviewReview the rules and exceptions
03
HR approvalUse the approved incentive figures
Illustrative workflow · not a client interface

Six modules. A five-level approval workflow.

  • Six operational modules with their own entry and calculation requirements.
  • A five-level approval workflow and role-based access.
  • Department reporting and a documented process for changes.

A working platform—and an estimate of capacity released.

The platform was implemented and confirmed active in writing by the client. It provides a concrete example of custom software built around a business process.

An owner-confirmed estimate puts annual repetitive work capacity released at approximately 876 person-days, using 6 × 365 × 0.40. This is an assumption-based capacity estimate, not a measured cash saving. Client identity is withheld.

The process is part of the product.

Agree the users, rules, exceptions and approval responsibilities together. A feature list alone does not describe the operation.
